Messages.Author: Joscha
Messages.Body:
Some time ago we talked in the Forum about some cards people saw as too strong and liked it to be changed.

We came to the conclusion that we should wait how the cards affect tournaments in the current season.

With the NAC and the EC played I think it's time to ask participating players and observers about what they think about that matter now.

I suggest that we sum up problematic cards first and talk about them in different threads.

In my opinion problematic cards are cards that doesn't fit the intended goals and the spirit of the game or that alter the game to an extreme degree. It is NOT about availability of cards.

So please if you observed problematic cards throughout this year tell us about it with a SHORT reason, why you think that card is bad for the game.

Please DON'T discuss it in this thread, I'd like to open up an extrathread per problematic card.

This is just for letting others know about your opinion. The decision if this card is altered, banned or stay the same is clearly up to the Rulesmonger Pascal Bertrand.

Baron of Frankfurt

Messages.Author: Izaak
Messages.Body:
#1 Lilith's Blessing - it makes everything you put on the table free. I would have liked the cardtext to be "choose a ready non-Bahari vampire you control with no Villein who has no blood ..."

#2 Giant's Blood - it turns the game into a lottery who gets to start with 40 pool. Also, if EVERY deck packs one, it's probably too good.

#3 Tupdog/Rock Cats in general. Not because it's broken per se, but because it disrupts tables beyond reason and needs very specific hosers to be stopped (Gran Madre, Tension).

#4 Maris Streck. No her special didn't really come into play during any games I played, but it really, really, should be once per action.

#5 Heart of Nizchetus. Also Heart of Timeout and Stalling.

That's the five I can think of. Of those, #1, #2 and #4 are just broken cards, whereas the other two have in my opinion such a negative effect on the actual playing of the game that something should be done about it.

Messages.Author: acbishop
Messages.Body:
Mainly I have to say that instead of thinking about nerfing cards we should think about clever deckmaking to stop people using broken cards.

Giant's Blood is ok like it is, it's only one every game, if everyone plays one it means that 4 people will discard a card cause someone 'd played it before, so for me no change needed.

Lilit's Blessing, I think that maybe Unique master would be perfect on it. Anyway, If everybody is able to put vampires in play is cause there are less people playing Sudden Reversal. One SR on Villein and you will avoid your prey having a free vampire. So let's play more Sudden Reversal.

Ashur + Liquidation, let's play more erciyes Fragment, trochomancy and other cards to stop those decks.

Maris Streck, she's great, she's powerful, but looking to the TWD archive, this year only 3 decks with her have won tournaments, I think you can find other vampires on more TWD (Nana Buruku for example) than Maris. So no need to change.

Heart of Nizchetus. if this pisses you off, play lots of cards able to destroy equipments, like Anarch troublemaker which is also helpful for killing your prey.

I think that we need to think about ways of building decks capable of dealing with those cards in a major tournament instead of thinking about nerfing them.

Just my 2 cents

Messages.Author: Joscha
Messages.Body:
My plan is to put up a short, straight discussion about one card each in which every interested VEKN-member can state his point of view ONCE and strengthen it with facts and arguments, followed by a poll with different options of nerfing and, most important, NO nerfing of course.

I'm tired of these 12 pages-threads where 3-5 people just repeat the obvious POVs and come to no decision. Maybe this time we can make clear statements and come to an end very soon with a poll. This poll doesn't guarantee anything of course, neither nerf or keep it that way. But it will hopefully be a valid score of the interested and caring players. Maybe the Rulesteam / Pascal Bertrand could keep these poll results in mind when deciding about cards.

So first a short discussion for about 7 days.
After that a poll about the suggested changes or no change for another 14 days.

You are free to let all players know of those polls. I'd be glad if you could place a hint in all forums.

The list of problematic cards so far:

1. Ashur Tablets
2. Villein
3. Lilith's Blessing
4. Giant's Blood
5. Maris Streck
6. Heart of Nizchetus
7. Parity Shift
8. Target Vitals
9. No Secrets from the Magaji
10. Tupdog
11. Liquidation

I try to be neutral here, but I don't want to discuss possibly every card in the game. We have to focus on real problems, otherwise this leads to nothing (again). Please try to be serious about this thread. I don't want you to mention cards like Voter Captivation or Immortal Grapple. We should limit this thread to cards which many players see a problem in.

Of course this also is a thread for the people, who don't want any change at all. Please don't try to counter every argument of the other participants in the following discussions. Just say why you like the card the way it is and vote in favour of no change. If you like to convince a poster I suggest to do it in PMs. My goal is to have a clear pro/contra thread, where a VEKN-member can follow the POVs and come to his own conclusions for the poll. I hope you all want that too.

I'd like to start the first thread for a card about Wednesday, because the players that participated in the EC need time to recover, allright?

Baron of Frankfurt

Messages.Author: AaronC
Messages.Body:
In the distant past of VTES, rules teams made changes to many cards that were either too strong or too weak, thus improving gameplay. We should be open to such revisions. My list:

1. Carlton van Wyck. He appears in every game I play. He is too cheap for what he does. He absorbs vampires' actions, usually with impunity. Most of my decks must spent significant resources to burn him in combat, usually 2 or 3 cards if they can do it at all. It should also not be possible to burn a diablerist by surprise by recruiting Carlton after the fact. Diablerie is already risky. I recently had two vampires burned by Carlton in the same game when he was brought back through Necromancy recursion. Suggested revision: 3 blood cost (minimum), and "During any Methusaleh's discard phase, you may burn Carlton to burn a vampire who has committed diablerie this turn."

2. Villein. According to reports, it was not playtested in its current form. Hoses Minion Tap while being better than Minion Tap. Day 1 Final of the EC timed out because of extensive Villein-related pool recursion - check out the tournament report on this site. Too powerful for a trifle. If I could go back and have input on the design, I would change the first sentence to "Put this card on a vampire you control and move 5 blood from that vampire to your pool." At the very least it should not hose Minion Tap so badly (which admittedly needed a bit of hosing).

3. Bounce cards. So you're being bled heavily by Malkavians, Toreadors, and/or any vampires with Dominate. Now you're also being bled heavily by other Methusalehs' vampires. I guess you should have played bounce yourself! Bounce is too cheap for what it can do. All bounce cards should reduce the redirected bleed by 1.

4. Target Vitals. This card has no requirements and no cost, but its effect is that of a card requiring a superior discipline, and a very good superior at that since it can affect ANY damage-dealing strike. Hands, weapons, thaumaturgy, bats: anything. Compare it to Potence strikes that CAN'T be used on guns or bats and that still allow an opponent to press, and that, say, require  to get +2 damage. Two damage is a lot, and it is often impossible or very costly to avoid the effect. Remove the "cannot press this round" clause at least. Since when do the undead have "vitals" anyway?

5. Lilith's Blessing. A storyline card that was not playtested, AFAIK. The combination with Villein is too stupid. At the least, Bahari should be a sect, causing the new Bahari to lose titles and anarch status.

6. Liquidation. A storyline card that was not playtested, AFAIK. 3 pool for free and you get to put cards in your ash heap to be recursed with copious tech? Really? At least remove the cards from the game.

7, 8. Heart of Nizchetus and Giant's Blood should cost at least one more pool than they do.

9. Parity Shift. I don't have a huge problem with it, but I think it should require a Primogen instead of a Prince or Justicar. This is an idea from Matt Wedge. This would immensely balance the power of Prince/Justicar decks with other decks, political and otherwise, and add welcome value to the primogen title. The idea also fits the source material as politically the Primogeniture maintainted the balance of power.

Wow, that rant felt good!

Messages.Author: PetriWessman
Messages.Body:
I wasn't at the EC this year (meh  ), but judging by what I've seen on the local scene over here:

1) Villein + Lilith's Blessing combo. Pretty much *every* deck packs this, and it's a bit ridiculous. Much better compact pool gain than anything else, with no requirements

2) Villein by itself. Something to make Minion Taps less good was warranted, but Villein went totally overboard. The number of Villeins in decks nowadays is... silly. Plus the lottery of who is able to do Villein + Giant's Blood first in the game (and get a huge advantage) is too random for my taste.

3) Ashur Tablets. Very good recursion with no requirements isn't something that the game needed.

4) Target Vitals. It's just too good. It's better than many discipline-based combat options, and it absolutely overshadows the other Target cards. It needs a nerf. Being able to cancel it with just one combat card might be a decent fix.

5) *Maybe* Lilith's Blessing by itself. It's very strong, and it should probably have been made a Unique. The main problem is the combo with Villein, though.

Other stuff I don't really see as a problem. Yes, Parity Shift is extremely strong, but it's a vote and there are multiple ways of dealing with those. Plus it requires a title, so you can see it coming. Yes, Maris Streck and the Heart of Cheating can slow down a game -- but there are tons of cards that can do that, it's not an isolated problem and imho doesn't make those cards into a problem.
